articles.title: Cuban Man in Miami Faces Charges for Filming Walmart Employee in Bathroom
articles.description: A 28-year-old Cuban national was taken into custody on Monday in southwest Miami-Dade, accused of taking photos and recording video of a Walmart employee inside a bathroom stall, as reported by the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office. The suspect, identified as Oscar Chamizo Martin, was caught around 12:15 p.m. at the store located at 14325 SW 268th St., in the Homestead area. He allegedly extended an orange-cased iPhone over the stall occupied by the victim. The Walmart employee noticed the device and, upon exiting the bathroom, confronted Chamizo Martin, who was the only individual present in that section at the time. Security cameras inside the Walmart recorded the employee leaving the restroom visibly distressed while calling for his manager. After the incident, Chamizo Martin left the store, but a sheriff's deputy contacted his employer and convinced him to return. Back at Walmart, the suspect denied taking any images, claiming someone else was responsible. However, he was found with an orange-cased iPhone that matched the victim's description exactly. Confronted with this evidence, he was arrested and taken to the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center (TGK), one of the main jail facilities in the county. As of Tuesday, Chamizo Martin remained detained with a $2,500 bond for the charge of digital voyeurism and also faced an immigration hold that could lead to deportation proceedings. In Florida, digital voyeurism is classified under statute 810.145, which prohibits the use of imaging devices to secretly record individuals in spaces where they have a reasonable expectation of privacy, like bathrooms or dressing rooms. For individuals over 19, the offense is considered a third-degree felony, punishable by up to five years in prison. This is not the first time Cuban nationals in Miami have faced serious criminal charges related to such behavior, amidst intensified cooperation between county authorities and federal immigration agencies. Florida has seen a series of voyeurism arrests in Walmart stores throughout 2025 and 2026 across various counties, including a recent case in Ocala just two days prior, where another man was apprehended for allegedly secretly recording minors in a similar setting. The immigration hold on Chamizo Martin indicates that immigration authorities have been notified of his arrest, which may result in additional consequences beyond the ongoing criminal proceedings.

articles.title: Man charged with burglary and voyeurism after allegedly trespassing into high school bathroom, stealing items
articles.description: LONE PEAK, Utah (ABC4) -- A man has been arrested and charged with burglary, voyeurism, and lewdness after he allegedly entered a high school, stole several items, walked into the women's bathroom, and urinated outside. Justin Lane Hopkins, 54, was charged with burglary (a third-degree felony), voyeurism, theft with prior convictions, possession of a dangerous weapon by a restricted person, criminal trespass, lewdness, and littering. According to charging documents, on Aug. 12, Lone Peak Police received a call of a potential trespass at Lone Peak High School. The alleged trespass happened two days earlier, and police claim video footage showed Hopkins entering the school building two separate times on the same day. Reportedly, Hopkins took several items from the building, including an hourglass, a book-shaped box, a can of soda, and a drawstring backpack. Police say the value of the items totaled approximately $500. Then, Hopkins allegedly opened an exterior door of the school and urinated, and shortly after that, he held the door open for someone to enter the building. Police also say that Hopkins entered a women's restroom inside the school twice while events were occurring and while there were people inside the school. Hopkins had previously been trespassed from the school, and signs throughout the building stated that visitors need to check in at the front office. After reviewing the footage, police found Hopkins in an encampment at Highland Glen Park. He allegedly admitted to entering the high school and taking items, and officers found the stolen items in his encampment. They also located a knife, and Hopkins reportedly acknowledged that he was on probation and that he wasn't supposed to have a knife. Police also noticed garbage around the camp, which was in a public park. Hopkins has a history of numerous drug-related convictions dating back to 2012. Most recently, he pleaded guilty to possession of a controlled substance in January 2025. Hopkins is being held in the Utah County Jail with bail. He had his initial court appearance on Monday, Aug. 17, and he has a waiver hearing scheduled for Aug. 26.

pendingReview.title: 'It's a peeping Tom': Pennsylvania police seek FBI, FAA help after drones hover outside bedroom windows
pendingReview.description: "I was hoping it was random, and then I started seeing them more and more often." What neighbors describe as recurring late-night drone activity in a Pennsylvania community is prompting fear, especially when the devices hover near sensitive parts of the house. According to WPVI, police say the reports are under investigation and that they are seeking help from federal authorities. Here's what to know In the Wallace area of West Brandywine Township, Pennsylvania, residents say drones have kept showing up over homes, the station said. The repeated sightings have raised privacy and safety worries, and some neighbors told police the aircraft have been seen near skylights as well as outside bedroom and bathroom windows. Police in West Brandywine said officers have also witnessed the activity and are handling the case as a possible privacy-related matter, according to WPVI. The department said it has notified the Federal Aviation Administration and contacted the FBI for help. An unnamed local resident said the activity is no longer a blip. "The first one came in December," she recalled, per WPVI. "I was hoping it was random, and then I started seeing them more and more often." More background Bradford Ryll, an aviation expert not involved in the case, noted to the station that operating a drone above a neighborhood is "not automatically illegal," because federal regulators control much of the airspace. "It is possible that if there is some kind of surveillance activity happening, that might be a violation of Pennsylvania law," he added to WPVI. For the unnamed resident, there's little ambiguity over what's happening. "If there was someone with a 20-foot ladder up to your windows looking in, would you be defending them?" she asked the station. "It's a peeping Tom; that's 100 percent what it is." She also told WPVI that she has tried to shield her home by putting in cameras and an alarm system, hanging drapes and blinds, and covering skylights to protect her privacy. What's being done? Police say the inquiry remains active and are urging residents to report additional sightings. In a statement provided to the station, the department said officers are taking the matter seriously. "The use of a drone to invade someone's personal privacy will not be tolerated, and the maximum allowable penalties will be pursued," they wrote. Jeff Kimes, chief of police and township fire marshal with the West Brandywine Police Department, asserted "residents deserve to feel safe and secure in their own homes," per WPVI. As the investigation continues and the police seek support from federal agencies, neighbors say they are still waiting for answers. "With four kids, the concern is there and very real as to why this person is hovering over our neighborhood," resident Shannon Kaschak said, per WPVI. pendingReview.title: 'It was horrifying': Woman's video leads to police arrest in Madison voyeurism case
pendingReview.description: MADISON, Ala. (WHNT) -- The quick actions of Alison Hoch led to the arrest of a man after a video she recorded appears to show him taking photos under her dress. Hoch said she went into the Once Upon A Child store in Madison, expecting a normal shopping trip for children's clothing. Instead, she said the trip took a strange turn when she felt a brush on her leg and became aware of a man standing near her. "Immediately, I didn't have a great gut feeling. He was standing pretty close to me," Hoch said. "But within a couple moments, I felt something very, very lightly brush the back of my leg." Hoch said she trusted that initial feeling and acted quickly, propping her phone up in her shopping cart and pressing record shortly after feeling the brush. That's when she captured troubling footage. The video appears to show a man looking underneath Hoch's dress and also taking multiple photographs underneath her skirt during the four and a half minute time span. Hoch was wearing a dress that had built-in shorts underneath. She told News 19 that she had no idea what he was doing at the time. "It was horrifying. It's a complete invasion of privacy. It's disturbing because I had no idea what he was doing while the video was going. Every time I turned around, it just looked like he was browsing," Hoch said. "I just saw the first time that he put his phone under and took a picture, and that's when I called 911." Hoch said she contacted police and kept the man in sight as he left the store. Madison Police said officers found James Curtis Coffey hiding in a nearby restaurant bathroom and retrieved his phone. Coffey was charged with voyeurism and taken to the Madison County Jail on August 12. Hoch said she hopes sharing this story will encourage other women to always be mindful of their surroundings. "You need to be excruciatingly aware of your situation," Hoch said. "Trust your gut. If something feels wrong, it's probably wrong." The investigation is ongoing, but the City of Madison said Coffey has bonded out of jail.

pendingReview.title: In 1890, a college student hid a camera in his vest, giving us the first candid look at Victorian life
pendingReview.description: Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. When we think of people in Victorian times, it's hard not to conjure up images of rigid poses and stoic, serious faces. After all, these were the images depicted in virtually every photograph from the time period. But thanks to one college student with a crush and a hidden camera, we do have a much more intimate glimpse into Victorian life. In 1893, Carl Størmer was 19 years old and studying mathematics at the Royal Frederick University (now the University of Oslo) when he did what so many men his age do: he fell smitten with a girl, and was too shy to approach her. A hidden camera with an unexpected purpose Wanting to capture a secret snapshot of his love interest, Størmer purchased a C.P. Stirn Concealed Vest Spy Camera: a device that looks something like a cartoonishly large pocketwatch, with a lens that can fit through a button hole, and a cable release that can be pulled through the pocket, allowing the user to take photos on the sly. While originally intended for general espionage and crime prevention, Størmer stumbled upon a different use for this spy camera. Not only did he successfully get a candid shot of his paramour, he got what we now refer to as "man on the street photos" of Victorian society. "I strolled down Carl Johan (street), found me a victim, greeted, got a gentle smile and pulled. Six images at a time and then I went home to switch the plate," he told the Hallvard Journal in 1942. Victorian life, but not as we usually imagine it Størmer produced more than 500 photographs depicting Victorians as we've never seen them before. Regular, everyday people grinning, relaxed, tipping their hats, eyeing Størmer suspiciously, a far cry from the posed and formal portraits we see in history books. In fact, aside from the attire, these people look like they could easily be plopped into our own timeline. That liveliness captured is what makes this collection feel so magical, and really not something we can get with previous eras that never even dreamt of this kind of technology. From street photos to scientific fame Størmer would go on to apply his passion for photography into his scientific work, where he made several significant contributions...the most notable to us normies being that he found a way to successfully photograph the Northern Lights. At nearly 70, Størmer would debut his fascinating collection of street photographs in its entirety -- previously he'd only shown a small portion -- and many of these can still be viewed today in Norway's Digitalt Museum. Recently, these photos were colorized and reanimated using AI software, making them feel like something out of a Gilded Age episode. As for the girl, a relationship between her and Størmer never culminated, but he would get to tell her years later of the role she unwittingly played in his legacy. Photography was an entirely new world Størmer wasn't the only man of his time period to blaze the photography trail, with Nikola Tesla experimenting with selfies and Eduard Spelterini trying his hand at aerial photography. One can only imagine the boundlessness felt as people explored this entirely new art form. And sure, photography continues to advance, but it's certainly something we take for granted now. Who could have guessed that one lovestruck college student with a hidden camera would accidentally give us a version of Victorian life we rarely get to see? But in the process, he also gave us a valuable lesson: that no matter the era, people will always be people. This article originally appeared in May. It has been updated.
